program_name: Stochastics and Data Science (Laurea Magistrale / M.Sc.)
teaching_language: Fully English-taught. This is a stand-alone degree programme entirely delivered in English (not an English pathway inside an Italian-named degree), and English is the official and working language of the M.Sc. Apply@UniTo lists 'Study language: English' and 120 ECTS over 2 years. It is a single-university UNITO degree (not an interuniversity/joint degree), although it is run jointly by three UNITO structures: the Department of Mathematics 'Giuseppe Peano' (administrative home), the ESOMAS Department (statistics) and the Department of Computer Science.
campus: Turin (Torino), Italy. Administering structure: Department of Mathematics 'Giuseppe Peano', University of Turin.
degree_class: LM-40 (Mathematics / Matematica). UNITO internal course code: 1203M22. [uncertain]
admission_type: Open access (no restricted number of places / 'numero programmato' does not apply), but admission is conditional on verification of the candidate's personal preparation. Apply@UniTo classifies it under the calls for 'open access postgraduate degree programs'. Verification is done through an online admission test, from which some candidates are exempted on the basis of their academic record. A separate territorial quota of 50 places applies to non-European applicants residing abroad. International applicants (holders of a foreign qualification) apply through the Apply@UniTo (DreamApply) portal; holders of an Italian degree apply through the domestic rounds published on the programme microsite.
application_deadline_eu: 8 September 2026, 23:59:59 CET - fourth admission call for open access postgraduate programmes, open 25 August - 8 September 2026, reserved to Italians, EU and EU-equivalent citizens and non-EU citizens legally residing in Italy. EU applicants may alternatively use the first (worldwide) call, 25 November 2025 - 29 January 2026. Note: the programme microsite additionally publishes a separate domestic round for holders of Italian degrees, reported as 27 August - 12 September 2026. [uncertain]
application_deadline_non_eu: 29 January 2026 - first admission call for the 2026/2027 academic year (portal opened 25 November 2025), the only call open to non-EU applicants residing abroad. The later 2026 calls are explicitly restricted to EU/EU-equivalent applicants and non-EU citizens legally residing in Italy ('This call is reserved to European applicants and non-EU applicants legally residing in Italy. If you apply without this prerequisite, your application will not be considered.'). Equivalent 2027/2028 dates were not yet published at the time of research.
entry_exam_or_test: Yes - an online admission test verifying the candidate's personal preparation, unless the candidate qualifies for an exemption. Documented format (as published for the most recent cycle for which the full text could be retrieved): online, 75 minutes, 4 parts - 10 multiple-choice questions each in Analysis, Probability and Statistics, plus 5 questions on English proficiency; all questions carry equal marks, no penalty for wrong answers; an overall score of at least 60% is required for admission. The Admission Committee reserves the right to also examine candidates orally after a successful test. Candidates are informed about their test participation about one week in advance, and further details are sent to applicants by e-mail. Exemption from the test is granted when condition A + B or A + C is satisfied: (A) the submitted current/previous studies include at least 20% of courses in Mathematics (for Italian degrees at least 36 CFU in mathematics sectors); (B) the candidate is still within the regular duration of the programme ('in corso') and all exams are completed at application time; or (C) the last degree was obtained no earlier than the calendar year before the application, either within the regular duration, or with at most one extra year and a final mark above 90% of the maximum (>99/110 for Italian degrees). Exempted candidates must still submit an admission application. In addition, at admission the Admission Committee uses the submitted documentation and an interview to assign each admitted student to Analysis Course A or Analysis Course B, in order to level students' background by the end of the first semester (this is a placement step, not a further selection). [uncertain]
academic_requirements: Entry qualification: a first-cycle degree (bachelor's / Laurea Triennale) obtained after at least 3 years of university education, or an equivalent or higher qualification. Apply@UniTo states the degree should be in Mathematics, Statistics or Physics, and that 'other degrees may be accepted, provided they offer the necessary background knowledge'. Candidates who have not yet graduated may apply if they can obtain the degree by the final enrolment deadline (typically the following December/January). Credit prerequisite: previous studies must include at least 20% of credits (36 CFU for Italian degrees) in the following disciplinary areas: Mathematics (MATH-*, formerly MAT/*), Statistics and mathematical methods for decisions (STAT-*, formerly SECS-S/*), Econometrics (ECON-05/A, formerly SECS-P/05), Computer Science / Information engineering (INFO-01/A and IINF/*, formerly INF/01 and ING-INF/*), Physics (PHYS-01/A and PHYS-02/A, formerly FIS/01-02). These credits may be cumulated across the listed areas and across multiple previous qualifications (e.g. a bachelor's plus a master's) and may include certified single courses/exams taken in addition to a degree. Applicants who do not meet the credit prerequisite are advised to attend and certify individual courses in the listed areas before applying. There is no fixed overall cap on admissions (open access, no restricted number of places) and no GPA/GRE/GMAT threshold is published; however, a territorial quota of 50 places applies to non-European applicants residing abroad. A motivation letter is a compulsory part of the application. Applicants holding several degrees must indicate in the application the degree most relevant to this programme. [uncertain]
language_requirements: English at minimum CEFR B2 level. Apply@UniTo states: 'Your knowledge of the English language (at least B2 level) will be verified during the admission procedure.' English proficiency is therefore assessed inside the admission process itself - the admission test includes a dedicated English proficiency section (5 questions) - so an external certificate is not stated as strictly mandatory on the official pages, but an English language certificate may be requested as one of the 'additional documents required by some specific postgraduate degree programmes'. Where UNITO requires a certificate it accepts IELTS, TOEFL iBT, Cambridge CPE/CAE/FCE, PTE Academic and Trinity College ISE II; Duolingo English Test is not accepted. No Italian language requirement applies for admission, since the programme is entirely in English (Italian is only useful for daily life; free Italian courses are offered by the University). Third-party aggregator sites quote a TOEFL iBT minimum of 87 for this programme, but this figure could not be confirmed on any official unito.it page. [uncertain]
required_documents: Via Apply@UniTo (postgraduate applicants): (1) entry qualification documents - bachelor's/first-cycle degree certificate and full transcript of records, or, for applicants close to graduating, proof of enrolment and exams passed; accepted in English, French, Italian or Spanish, otherwise the original plus a certified translation; (2) documents required for the applicant's specific foreign education system (per the Apply@UniTo 'Required documentation' page); (3) a motivation letter in English or Italian (compulsory for all postgraduate programmes and explicitly listed under 'Other requirements' for this programme); (4) additional programme-specific documents referred to under 'Entry qualification', 'Language requirements' and 'Other requirements' - for this programme, evidence of the minimum credit requirement in the listed disciplinary areas and, where applicable, an English language certificate; (5) optional but recommended: the degree programme syllabus / course descriptions issued by the foreign institution, translated into Italian, English, French or Spanish (this also supports a request for exemption from the admission test); (6) identity document/passport. A non-refundable application fee of EUR 60 must be paid within the deadline of the call (the same amount whether one or two programmes are selected). After submission, UNITO may request further documents such as a Declaration of Value, Statement of Verification or CIMEA Statement of Comparability, and the International Students Office may request additional documents at the enrolment stage. [uncertain]

uncertainty_notes: 1) ACCESS LIMITATIONS: www.master-sds.unito.it, www.unito.it and en.unito.it refuse direct connections from this environment (connection refused / 403), and r.jina.ai is behind a Cloudflare challenge. Fully verified primary content therefore comes from apply.unito.it (fetched directly, including its JSON feed) plus an Internet Archive capture of the programme's Admissions page. The most recent Wayback capture available for that Admissions page is from 15 June 2024 and describes a.y. 2024/25; the detailed test format, 60% threshold and exemption conditions are quoted from that capture. Live search-engine snippets of the same page confirm the 20%/36 CFU prerequisite, the 60% test threshold, the exemption rounds statement, the Analysis A/B interview step and a 2026 domestic application window, which indicates the structure is unchanged for 2026/27, but the exact 2026/27 wording, test dates and feedback dates could not be read in full. 2) DISCIPLINARY SECTOR CODES: the archived page lists the old Italian SSD codes (MAT/*, SECS-S/*, SECS-P/05, INF/01, ING-INF/*, FIS/01-02) while live snippets show the new codes (MATH-*, STAT-*, ECON-05/A, INFO-01/A, IINF/*, PHYS-01/A, PHYS-02/A). Both have been listed; the new codes are the current ones. 3) TWO PARALLEL APPLICATION TRACKS: holders of a foreign qualification apply via Apply@UniTo (calls: 25 Nov 2025 - 29 Jan 2026 worldwide; 25 Aug - 8 Sep 2026 EU/EU-equivalent/legally resident in Italy only), while holders of an Italian degree apply through separate domestic rounds run by the programme itself, whose 2026 window is reported by search snippets as 27 August - 12 September 2026. These two calendars must not be conflated; the domestic window date is taken from a search snippet and is marked uncertain. 4) DEGREE CLASS: LM-40 and course code 1203M22 come from official UNITO/CINECA catalogue titles and AlmaLaurea, but the exact 2026/27 catalogue page could not be opened (CINECA catalogue returned HTTP 405). 5) ENGLISH CERTIFICATE: no official minimum test score is published on unito.it for this programme; the requirement is stated as 'at least B2, verified during the admission procedure'. The TOEFL iBT 87 figure circulating on aggregator sites (Mastersportal) is NOT confirmed by any official source and should not be treated as an official threshold. 6) NON-EU QUOTA: the figure of 50 places for non-European applicants residing abroad comes from the Apply@UniTo course page; it is a territorial quota and does not make the programme restricted-access overall. 7) 2027/2028 CYCLE: as of the research date (1 September 2026) only 2026/2027 calls were published; deadlines for the following cycle were not yet available.
